result.topic_en: Euler derives a formula for the apparent angle that the Moon's orbit makes with the ecliptic during a lunar eclipse, measured relative to the Earth's shadow, and then begins giving mean hourly motions of the Sun and Moon from tables.
result.transcription:
De loco lunae ex eclipsibus lunaribus determinando. 375
§ 24. Interest deinde etiam in contemplatione eclipsium nosse angulum apparentem, quem [orbita] [?] lunae cum ecliptica constituit. Hic scilicet centrum umbrae in ecliptica tanquam immobile [spectatur] [?], et angulus quaeritur, quem luna in orbita sua secundum motum relativum cum ecliptica [format] [?]. Ad hunc inveniendum sit (Fig. 206) $\sigma$ centrum umbrae in vera oppositione, et $\lambda$ centrum [lunae] [?], ita ut arcus $\lambda\sigma$ sit ad eclipticam perpendicularis. Sit ut hactenus, medio eclipsis momento [longitudo] [?] umbrae a nodo $= x$, erit ut vidimus in vera oppositione arcus
$$☊\sigma = x + \frac{2(m+k)(n+k)}{g(n-m)^2}\sin 2x \,\mathrm{tang}^2 \tfrac{1}{2}\rho = x + d,$$
posito brevitatis gratia
$$d = \frac{2(m+k)(n+k)}{g(n-m)^2}\sin 2x\,\mathrm{tang}^2\tfrac{1}{2}\rho.$$
Jam tempusculo infinite parvo procedat centrum umbrae per spatiolum $\sigma s = u$, et luna per $\lambda l = \nu u$, [existente] [?] $\nu = \frac{n+k}{m+k}$. Ponatur angulus $☊\lambda\sigma = \varphi$, erit $\cos\varphi = \cos(x+d)\sin\rho = \cos x\sin\rho - gd\sin x\sin\rho$. Jam ex $l$ in $\sigma\lambda$ productum demittatur perpendiculum $lu$, erit ob $\lambda l$ infinite parvum,
$$lu = \nu u\sin\varphi \quad\text{et}\quad \lambda u = \nu u\cos\varphi = \nu u(\cos x\sin\rho - gd\sin x\sin\rho);$$
[porro erit] [?]
$$\sin^2\varphi = 1 - \cos^2 x\sin^2\rho + 2gd\sin x\cos x\sin^2\rho,$$
ideoque ob $\sin^2\rho$ valde parvum
$$\sin\varphi = \cos\rho + \tfrac{1}{2}\sin^2 x\sin\rho\,\mathrm{tang}\,\rho + gd\sin 2x\sin\rho\,\mathrm{tang}\,\rho.$$
§ 25. Jam ad motum relativum repraesentandum removeamus totum systema motu sibi parallelo, [ut] [?] punctum $s$ perveniat in $\sigma$, et $l$ in $t$, eritque $t$ locus centri lunae ex centro umbrae $\sigma$ spectatus, [ideoque] [?] interea centrum lunae ex $\lambda$ in $t$ pervenisse et arcum $\lambda t$ descripsisse censebitur; ac propterea angulus $\lambda tu$ erit ille angulus, quem orbita lunae apparens cum ecliptica facere videbitur; erit autem [$lt = u$] [?], ideoque $tu = \nu u\sin\varphi - u$. Quare ob $\lambda u = \nu u\cos\varphi$, reperietur tangens anguli quaesiti $ut\lambda$, [nempe] [?]
$$\mathrm{tang}\, ut\lambda = \frac{\nu\cos\varphi}{\nu\sin\varphi - 1} = \frac{(n+k)\cos\varphi}{(n+k)\sin\varphi - m - k}, \text{ seu } = \frac{(n+k)\sin\rho(\cos x - gd\sin x)}{(n+k)\cos\rho + \frac{1}{2}(n+k)\sin^2 x\sin\rho\,\mathrm{tang}\,\rho - m - k}.$$
[Facilius] [?] autem hic angulus reperietur ex angulo $\varphi$, quem ante investigari oportebit, ex formula [$\cos\varphi$] [?] $= \cos(x+d)\sin\rho$, existente
$$d = \frac{2(m+k)(n+k)}{g(n-m)^2}\sin 2x\,\mathrm{tang}^2\tfrac{1}{2}\rho;$$
[et posito] [?] $\nu = \frac{n+k}{m+k}$ erit tang. anguli quaesiti $= \frac{\nu\cos\varphi}{\nu\sin\varphi - 1}$. Potest quoque particula $d$ prorsus [negligi, cum] [?] perinde sit, sive ista inclinatio apparens ad medium eclipsis momentum, sive ad veram oppositionem supputetur.
§ 26. Quo igitur has formulas in usum vocare queamus, requiritur, ut tempore eclipsis veros [motus] [?] horarios tam lunae quam solis et nodi cognoscamus, cui investigationi sequens caput est [destinatum] [?]. Interim tamen juvabit hic valorem medium horum motuum perpendisse. Ex tabulis astronomicis invenimus motum medium horarium solis $m = 2'27''50''' = 147\tfrac{5}{6}'' = 147'',833$; [motum] [?] medium horarium lunae $n = 32'56''28''' = 1976\tfrac{7}{15}'' = 1976'',4666$, et motum horarium

items.quote: Interest deinde etiam in contemplatione eclipsium nosse angulum apparentem, quem [orbita] [?] lunae cum ecliptica constituit.
items.english: It is further important, in the study of eclipses, to know the apparent angle which the Moon's orbit makes with the ecliptic.

items.quote: Potest quoque particula $d$ prorsus [negligi, cum] [?] perinde sit, sive ista inclinatio apparens ad medium eclipsis momentum, sive ad veram oppositionem supputetur.
items.english: The small quantity d may also be neglected entirely, since it makes no difference whether this apparent inclination is computed for the middle moment of the eclipse or for the true opposition.

items.quote: requiritur, ut tempore eclipsis veros [motus] [?] horarios tam lunae quam solis et nodi cognoscamus, cui investigationi sequens caput est [destinatum] [?].
items.english: It is required that we know the true hourly motions of the Moon, the Sun and the node at the time of the eclipse; the following chapter is devoted to this investigation.
